gaps.sentence: You ___ decide now — take your time and think it over.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' removes the obligation to act immediately: needn't decide.

gaps.sentence: Applications ___ be submitted in person, not by post.
You ___ not be so hard on yourself — everyone makes mistakes.
gaps.explanation: 'Should not' gives gentle advice against something: should not be.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better take some cash — the stall does not take cards.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' warns about a sensible action: had better take.

gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: It ___ be the postman — he has already been this morning.
gaps.hint: ruled out by what already happened
gaps.explanation: Evidence that rules something out uses 'can't': can't be.

gaps.hint: a polite offer with would you like
gaps.explanation: 'Would you like' makes a polite offer: Would.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.
